title: Publisher integration playbook: marketplace QA & copy
content:
Purpose:
This playbook is a concise, technical-first checklist + copy bank to accelerate partner listings on cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace). Target audience: partner engineering, partner PMs, and internal GTM/ops who coordinate publishing. It prioritizes artifacts that commonly block publish: example integration tests, security attestations, and canonical copy variants optimized for enterprise buyers.

High-level flow (recommended timeline):
- Day 0: Kickoff call (partner, partner-eng, GTM owner) — share this playbook and stub assets.
- D1–D5: Partner provides baseline assets (icons, screenshots, short/long descriptions, pricing model).
- D6–D12: Partner engineering runs guided integration tests and returns evidence.
- D13–D20: GTM reviews copy, compliance, and pricing; legal/do-not-sell checks.
- D21+: Marketplace submission and iterative fixes. Expect 2–6 week total depending on partner responsiveness and marketplace backlog.

Required technical artifacts (must-have before submission):
- API endpoint checklist: base URL, health check, sample request/response, supported auth (API key/OAuth).
- SDK / integration sample: short README + 1 minimal code sample for Python/Node showing host + key usage.
- Integration tests: one smoke test demonstrating model inference (text generation or embeddings) that runs in <=30s. Include test logs and exact commands.
- Billing/pricing matrix: SKU IDs, unit (per-token, per-embed, seats), trial credits config, and meter-reporting docs.
- Security bundle: SOC2 summary OR attestation, data flow diagram (png), privacy policy link, encryption at-rest/in-transit notes, KMS integration docs if applicable.
- Support & SLAs: Support contact, hours, expected TTR for Sev1/Sev2, and optional premium SLA text.
- Images & assets: 1024x1024 app icon PNG, 3 screenshots (1200x800) with captions, and 1 product logo SVG.

Acceptance criteria / QA gates (internal):
- Functional: smoke test executes with documented output and no auth failures.
- Security: privacy & encryption statements present; any 3rd-party data processors declared.
- Billing: SKU mapping validated with finance (sample invoice or simulated meter).
- Copy: short + long descriptions pass tone/length checks below.
- Images: icons/screenshots meet size, transparency, and content guidelines.

Marketplace copy bank (use as a source; adapt tone per marketplace):
- Short tagline (<=140 chars):
  "Low-latency, cost-aware LLM inference — hosted, dedicated, or private deployment options for production teams."

- Elevator (1–2 lines):
  "Redwood Inference delivers predictable, high-throughput LLM serving with built-in observability and cost controls. Ship rich LLM features without rebuilding inference infra."

- Long description (3–4 paragraphs, enterprise-friendly):
  "Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that helps engineering teams deliver LLM-powered features at production scale. Choose hosted, dedicated GPU pools, or private VPC/on-prem deployment while preserving a consistent API and tooling surface.

  The platform focuses on predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and reliability. Built-in features include streaming responses, function calling, KV prefix caching, and per-route observability that ties quality regressions to prompt sets and evals.

  For enterprises, Redwood offers reserved capacity contracts, private control plane options, KMS/HSM key integrations, and audit logging to meet compliance requirements. Our rollout tooling supports canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants when needed.

  Getting started is simple: use our REST or SDK clients to evaluate with free credits, or follow the included sample integration that runs a smoke inference in under 30 seconds."

Tone & length guidelines: keep short tagline <=140 chars; elevator <= 2 sentences; long description 400–700 chars per paragraph as needed; avoid marketing superlatives without measurable claims (e.g., "fastest" requires benchmark link).

Common blockers and mitigations: 
- Missing billing SKU mapping — mitigation: schedule a 30-min call with finance and partner to map usage to marketplace metering.
- Incomplete smoke test due to auth issues — mitigation: provide a dedicated ephemeral API key and sample curl request; include exact header names.
- Security docs lagging — mitigation: accept interim SOC2 summary + date, require full report pre-production.

Submission checklist (before hitting submit):
- [ ] Short tagline (finalized)
- [ ] Long description (finalized)
- [ ] 1024x1024 icon PNG
- [ ] 3 screenshots + captions
- [ ] 1 SVG logo
- [ ] SKU/pricing matrix in vendor format
- [ ] Support & SLA blurb
- [ ] Smoke test artifacts + logs
- [ ] Security bundle or attestation
- [ ] Legal contact + export control review (if applicable)

Suggested staging & rollout plan post-acceptance:
- Private listing + test tenant (internal) — verify metering, entitlement checks, and deployment duplication.
- Soft launch to pilot customers (<10) for 2 weeks to monitor usage and billing alignment.
- Enabled observability: add token-level cost dashboards and per-route latency heatmaps in Redwood Console.

Example minimal integration test (one-line description for partner eng):
- "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'" — include response body and timing.

Notes / open questions to resolve with partner: 
- Do they require dedicated GPU marketplace SKU vs hosted?
- Is customer data routed through partner systems (data-flow implications)?
- Are there export-control or regional restrictions for the model weights?
